retell: Honey fakers were cutting real honey with cheap rice syrup and paying labs to tune their blends until they beat Europe's tests, until EU scientists brought sharper tests and found almost half the imports were suspected fake, not the one in seven everyone thought.
twist: The fakers weren't just slipping past the tests by luck. They paid labs to test their own blends and tuned the syrup until it beat the checks, so the old 'one in seven' figure was a number they had gamed.
payoff: Yes. The title promises 'almost half' and line 1 promises 'the real share was worse'. Line 5 delivers exactly that: almost half, three times the old count. It then turns it on the viewer with 'What's in your jar?' The cost is that the title already gives the ending away, so the payoff confirms what you were told instead of surprising you.
chain: It holds. Line 2 gives the motive behind the faking in line 1. Line 3 follows from it ('So they pay labs'). Line 4 turns against it ('But' sharper tests). Line 5 is the result of line 4. No line is just 'and here is another fact'.
problems: The title and line 1 both give away the ending ('almost half', 'worse'), so the reveal in line 5 has less punch than it could. A title that teases the cat-and-mouse ('Honey fakers were beating the tests') would hold the number back.
Line 2's 'every spoonful is profit' is a generic phrase. The cost gap is the motive, but it doesn't show anything an animated character could act out in a vivid way.
Line 4 is the weakest beat to picture. 'Sharper tests' is abstract, with no hint of what changed, so the turning point lands on wording instead of on something you can see.
